lakes.name: Lake Burullus
lakes.location: the northern Nile Delta coast, Kafr El-Sheikh Governorate
lakes.summary: a shallow brackish coastal lagoon separated from the Mediterranean by a sand bar, with a narrow outlet to the sea
lakes.history: It is fed mainly by agricultural drains from the Delta, and its shores are lined with fish farms, reed beds and reclaimed farmland.

items.text: A shallow brackish lagoon on the northern Nile Delta coast, connected to the Mediterranean by a narrow outlet and fed mainly by agricultural drains.
Reported to vary across the lake: generally fresher near drain inflows and saltier near the sea outlet.
Surrounding Delta soils are mainly Nile alluvium used for agriculture; salt-affected soils are reported along parts of the northern fringe.
Fish farms and reclaimed land have been reported along parts of the shoreline, and fishing is an important local livelihood.
